Q: What is the use case of useMemo in React? A:

As answered by Philip, It is correct that you can use both the useEffect() and useMemo() for achieving the same result at the end.

But the primary intention for creating useMemo() hook is to store computationally intensive functions and the primary intention for creation of useEffect() is to do some side effects like fetching data, or doing something in background which may or may not re render something like subscribing to event.

Now we can use both for other purposes, but useMemo is used when we want to render the value in the initial render itself, and useEffect is used to re render after a initial render, when background tasks to be done are time taking, as to provide good user experience.

So it's basically your choice to choose depending upon what type of task you are doing when you want to render that data.

Q: Stop Space-completion, but keep Tab-completion in Visual Studio Community 2026 for C++ A:

I've got it to work again (in version 18.9.2) with the following (seemingly almost random) settings:

in All Settings -> Languages -> C/C++ -> IntelliSense -> Completion list

  • select "Commit the item by pressing one of the commit characters"

  • deselct "When an item is highlighted but not selected commit the item by pressing Tab or Space"

in All Settings -> Text Editor -> Advanced

  • set "Default IntelliSense completion mode" to "Tab-only"

/edit this unfortunately only fixes it for some situations. not all.

There's no more autocomplete on [space] in the following situations:

  • namespace autocompletes (i.e. something like std::c[space])

  • #include stuff (see comment by Chris below)
    #incl[space]
    #include <iostr[space]

  • no autocomplete on new class members
    struct MyClass {int myMember{}; };
    main() { MyClass test{}; test.someNewVar[space]}
    no longer replaces someNewVar with some member of test

But it still autocompletes on [space] for

  • struct MyClass {int myMember{}; };
    main() { MyClass test{}; test.m[space] }

Q: When modifying ("modding") a game I get Error CS1061 in reference to code from "From The Depths Try 2" A:

You say "I then renamed things in a new class", but you did more than that, or lets say, you renamed things you can't rename.

Specifically, you changed the line:

base.MainConstruct.iBlockTypeStorage.PlasmaMantletStore.Add(this);

to:

base.MainConstruct.iBlockTypeStorage.HeavyPlasmaMantletStore.Add(this);

Which probably is the source of "IBlockToConstructBlockTypeStorage has no accessible method HeavyPlasmaMantletStore".

How do you fix this?

iBlockTypeStorage, as a property of MainConstruct has a type, and a type has methods and attributes you can access. You cannot change those methods and attributes (unless you change the code of iBlockTypeStorage). Work with documentation, IDE-hints and code to figure out which methods and attributes exist, and compile and test often and after every little change, so you know more easily where the problem is.

Now, how to actually add a store to this specific game with modding, I don't know. This is just a troubleshooting guide on your programming problem, hope it helps.

Q: How to delete old executions and jobs from rundeck A:

i had the same problem and the rd-cli is to slow. in my solution i get the older execution ids directly from the rundeck database and use a http request to the rundeck-api to bulk delete 200 execution-records and referenced log-files at once. All you need is to configure an api-token:

RD_TOKEN=....
RD_URL=https://your.rundeckhost

# condition: executions older than 1 month in the past

curl -X POST -H "X-Rundeck-Auth-Token: $RD_TOKEN" \

      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \

      -d '{"ids":["'$(mysql rundeck -e "

        SELECT id FROM execution

        where date_started < '$(date --date="1 months ago" +"%Y-%m-%d")'

        limit 200 ;" -B|sed 1d|perl -0ne 's/\n$//;s/\n/","/g;print')'"]}' "${RD_URL}/api/40/executions/delete"

In detail:

sql-statement to get executions:

        use rundeck;
 
        SELECT id FROM execution 
        where date_started < '2026-08-01'
        limit 5 ;

sql from bash:


mysql rundeck -e "SELECT id FROM execution 
        where date_started < '$(date --date="1 months ago" +"%Y-%m-%d")'
        limit 5 ;"

batch output without header-line:

mysql rundeck -e "SELECT id FROM execution 
        where date_started < '$(date --date="1 months ago" +"%Y-%m-%d")'
        limit 5 ;" -B|sed 1d

preparing for json array:

mysql rundeck -e "SELECT id FROM execution 
        where date_started < '$(date --date="1 months ago" +"%Y-%m-%d")'
        limit 5 ;" -B|sed 1d|perl -0ne 's/\n$//;s/\n/","/g;print'

        
echo '{"ids":["'$(mysql rundeck -e "SELECT id FROM execution 
        where date_started < '$(date --date="1 months ago" +"%Y-%m-%d")'
        limit 5 ;" -B|sed 1d|perl -0ne 's/\n$//;s/\n/","/g;print')'"]}'

all at once:

time curl -X POST -H "X-Rundeck-Auth-Token: $RD_TOKEN" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{"ids":["'$(mysql rundeck -e "
        SELECT id FROM execution 
        where date_started < '$(date --date="1 months ago" +"%Y-%m-%d")'
        limit 5 ;" -B|sed 1d|perl -0ne 's/\n$//;s/\n/","/g;print')'"]}' "${RD_URL}/api/40/executions/delete"

i also made a youtube video out of it: https://youtu.be/XMA-WpqzgvI?si=29cBw9238wrkNlPb

keep in mind, that the api-url may be different depending to your rundeck-version

Q: How to fetch a realTime news Data feed A:

Scraping is theoretically an option but most such data will be under license. If you take it without correct permissions or process you may leave yourself open to legal action, and also bigger sites nowadays often have good defences which will make scraping by bots difficult or impossible. And such a method is unlikely to be any faster than RSS anyway.

If your research doesn't reveal any suitable free/public options then approach a news organisation whose data you want to use and see if they have any commercial arrangements you can make to subscribe to real-time data.
